newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SAirGroup targets 600 mln Sfr 1997 EBIT.
newsitem.headline: SAirGroup targets 600 mln Sfr 1997 EBIT.

text.p: SAirGroup, the group that includes the Swissair airline, is targeting sharply higher operating profits of 600 million Swiss francs ($410 million) in 1997 after reaching 155 million in the first four months.

The target -- never publicly announced before -- was published in an article in SAirGroup's internal magazine, SAirGroup News, which detailed the outcome of a recent meeting of SAirGroup managers in Montreaux.
"Of the 600 million francs, which we should have on the books by the end of the year, only 155 million have been earned," the magazine quoted SAirGroup chief executive Philippe Bruggisser as saying.
Bruggisser was commenting on SAirGroup's performance in the January-April period and also said the group was ahead of budget in that period, the first time in a long time.
A SAirGroup spokesman confirmed the target, adding it referred to operating earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT).
He also confirmed that SAirGroup had not announced such a target to the press before.
Analysts are generally optimistic about SAirGroup's performance this year based on better performance by its airline operations and results from its restructuring programme.
SAirGroup will release first half results on August 21 and the spokesman said he could not make any comments on how business developed since the end of April.

In a recent study analyst Urs Kunz of Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB) forecast a six-month EBIT of around 190 million francs, up from 20 million in the first half of 1996, and a net profit of around 80 million, up from a loss of 51 million.
For 1997 Kunz is forecasting an EBIT of 540 million and a net profit of 270 million.
In 1996 SAirGroup reported an operating profit of 344 million francs, up from 1995's 247 million, but extraordinary charges of 739 million francs produced a net loss of 497 million.
SAirGroup's official forecast for 1997 calls for a higher operating profit, but at the company's annual news conference in April officials declined to be more specific.
A 1997 EBIT of 600 million Swiss francs implies that SAirGroup expects its operating profit to rise 74 percent from 1996's 344 million.
In May SAirGroup chairman Hannes Goetz told the annual shareholders' meeting that business in the first four months of 1997 had lived up to and in most areas exceeded its targets.
On Monday Swissair's new chief operating officer Jeffrey Katz also said it looked like the first half result would be good for the airline.
